messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@obsidian.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed pilot runway (next steps)

Elena — great conversation earlier today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the pilot: 

Summary of pain we heard
- High false-positive rate in their triage assistant (NLP classifier) when customer messages contain domain-specific jargon.
- Current in-house rerank is costly per request and has burst latency that breaks SLAs for live agents.

Goals for a successful pilot (30 days)
1) Bring false-positive rate down by 30% on the 3 most common intents (billing dispute, refund request, product outage).
2) Maintain median inference latency <= 220ms for 512-token requests under expected pilot load (~50rps burst to 150rps).
3) Demonstrate a 20% reduction in token cost using Redwood batching + prefix cache in typical prompt flows.

Proposed scope and success metrics
- Model: open-model baseline you run today -> we’ll serve equivalent and a quantized low-cost variant; compare quality and latency.
- Eval set: 2k-3k anonymized customer messages from your June–Dec 2025 window (we agreed to a 2k initial sample).
- Metrics: precision/recall per intent, median P95 latency, and tokens-per-response cost.

Ownership / roles
- Obsidian: Elena (product lead) — will provide data access + anonymized eval set; Tom (eng) — provide AWS read-only role and SSO admin contact for Redwood Private if needed.
- Redwood: Aditya — engagement lead; Monica — CS/ops lead; Marcus — SRE/SE for access and performance tuning.

Timeline (proposed, flexible)
- Week 0 (this week): sign MOP / MOU, exchange access details, share eval CSV.
- Week 1: pilot environment provisioned, prompt set upload, initial model comparisons.
- Week 2: run evals, iterate prompts, early latency tuning.
- Week 3–4: stabilization, quality review, final readout + decision.

Access needed from you this week
1) Eval dataset (anonymized CSV) — drop in the S3 bucket or share via secure Drive link.
2) An IAM role ARN with s3:GetObject on the eval bucket, or a file transfer link.
3) Point-of-contact for procurement/legal: contracts@obsidian.ai (you mentioned).

Attachments: attached a short mutual action plan and a suggested prompt-eval template to make the sample-run quick.

If this matches what you heard, reply with agreed kickoff date (happy to start as early as next Tuesday) and confirm the S3 path + IAM contact.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

— Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items and a couple of clarifying questions: 

1) The 2k eval sample is fine — we will anonymize and remove PII. I’ll aim to have that in an S3 path by Monday EOD (s3://obsidian-pilot/eval/initial.csv).
2) Tom will create an IAM role with read-only access and send the ARN to you.
3) Procurement: forwarding to contracts@obsidian.ai — they’ll handle the MOU and review the standard terms.

Clarifying questions: 
- For the latency target you listed (median <= 220ms), is that for the hosted Redwood API or for a Private deployment? We need to set correct expectations — our infra team prefers Private for data controls but we can do a short hosted run first.
- On metric calc: are you using strict intent labels or a soft-match threshold (we prefer to see both).

We’re good to start next Tuesday (20 Jan) if Redwood can confirm provisioning timeline.

Thanks,
Elena
Product Lead, Obsidian Analytics
